answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 25 money. 2. Take four workers: one active on the notepad and three inactive/lying down below it. 3. Draw eight Zoo cards and keep four, discarding the other four to a face-up discard pile. 4. Draw two Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden beside your map. 5. Put Animals side I in slot 1; place the other four side-I Action cards randomly in slots 2–5. 6. Appeal starts at 0 for the starting player, then 1, 2 and 3 in turn order.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C3, D, E, F; B; C1: stagger by turn order: start player on space 0 ... fourth on space 3.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the Base Conservation Project cards; put four face up below the Association board in a four-player game and three in two- or three-player games. 2. Only in a two-player game, use six tokens of an unused color to block the left level of the left base card, middle level of the middle card, right level of the right card, and the three spaces in the donation area's left column; these are unavailable to both players. 3. Three-player games have three projects and no stated blocked spaces; four-player games have four projects and no stated blocked spaces. 4. Reveal the initial six-card display only after all players have selected their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c; Personal setup G: after everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards.

answers.answer: 1. After using a card in slot 4, remove it, shift cards in slots 1–3 one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set strength before beginning the action; each X-token spent adds 1 strength, and X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. 3. You may spend any number, subject to the maximum of five X-tokens held. 4. Resolve an 'after finishing' effect only after completing the action and moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove the card ... shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right ... place the used card in slot 1; strength before performing; each token ... +1; max 5; after finishing includes moving Action cards.

answers.answer: 1. No: you may not do nothing, and playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not a legal action. 2. The alternative X-token action lets you choose an Action card, take exactly one X-token, move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right; strength and upgrade state do not matter. 3. You cannot use this alternative when you already hold five X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Taking a turn: You may not do nothing ... Use the alternative X-token action; X-token action: take exactly 1 ... slot's strength ... irrelevant ... If ... already have 5 ... cannot.

answers.answer: 1. Ignore Break-track steps beyond its last space. 2. The player who reaches the last space gains one X-token. 3. Finish the current turn; the break then happens for everyone. 4. After the break the token returns to the starting space. The summary's additional-final-turn rule applies only if the game end is triggered: after a break-triggered end, all players take one more turn; it does not say a break by itself grants that turn.
answers.evidence: When it reaches the last space ... break ... after the end of your current turn, and you get 1 X-token ... Ignore any additional steps ... after the break ... returns; normal break alone does not give any extra turns.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I advances the Break token two spaces, then either draws from the deck by its strength table (up to three cards, with any required discard) or, at strength 5+, snaps exactly one card of your choice from the display regardless of reputation; a snap is not a deck draw. 2. Cards II also advances two spaces, then draws from the deck and/or display cards within reputation range in any order using its upgraded table; at strength 5, for example, take four and discard one. 3. Cards II snap threshold is strength 3+, and a snap takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation, with no deck draw. 4. On side II only the display-draw option is reputation-limited. 5. Cards I display snap replenishes at end of turn; side II display cards are not replenished until the turn is complete. 6. Hand size is unlimited during turns and is checked only at breaks, when you discard down to your limit.
answers.evidence: CARDS action: side I ... 2 spaces ... draw ... or snap ... side II ... in any order ... snapping ... strength 3 ... reputation restriction applies only ... display ... not replenished until turn complete; no in-turn hand limit.

answers.answer: 1. Reputation range includes the display folder matching your current reputation and every lower-numbered folder. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action. 3. At reputation 15, each additional reputation step instead gives one appeal; the counter remains at 15. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: 'Within reputation range' = ... matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders; Reputation 10+ requires upgraded Cards; on 15 ... 1 appeal per remaining step; may not look through discard pile.

answers.answer: 1. Build I builds exactly one building, size no greater than strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings whose total size is at most strength, but never two identical buildings in that action. 2. Pay two money per space/size before placing each building. 3. The first building must have at least one space on a border space; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. 4. Build only on empty spaces within the map and do not cover rock or water; spaces with the restricted icon require upgraded Build. 5. Kiosks must be at least three spaces apart from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion immediately raises appeal by one, once when built.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: exactly 1 ... size ... cost ... placement rules ... first building ... border ... restricted icon ... kiosk ... Each pavilion ... appeal by 1.

answers.answer: 1. Build I can build standard enclosures of sizes 1–5, a kiosk, pavilion, or one Petting Zoo (size 3). Build II additionally allows a Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary, each size 5. 2. The supply contains four tiles of each special enclosure type; each zoo may contain at most one of each type. 3. Build never creates unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 4. When every map space except water and rock is covered, immediately gain seven appeal; Build II opens restricted-icon spaces, though coverage by another effect can also complete the map.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table; supply has four tiles ... each individual zoo ... one; Unique buildings can never be built with this action; full map ... gain 7 appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Yes: bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. 2. Immediate effects resolve when triggered, including between animals or buildings; 'after finishing' effects wait until the whole action is complete and the Action card has moved. 3. If effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Bonuses gained earlier ... may be used for later steps ... pay each item before receiving its own benefits; animal effects ... immediately ... after finishing ...; multiple simultaneous effects ... choose the order.

answers.answer: 1. For each animal, meet every left-side condition and pay its printed cost; a partner zoo on its continent reduces cost by three money per continent icon printed on that animal, including double icons (six total reduction for two). Pay before any gain-money play effect. 2. Put an animal in an empty standard enclosure meeting its printed minimum size and flip that entire enclosure to occupied; it normally holds one animal. Except Petting Zoo animals, animals may use a suitable standard enclosure. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. 3. Eligible reptiles and birds may instead use their corresponding Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary; place one supply token per indicated occupied space and do not flip the special enclosure. Observe free capacity. 4. Meet required adjacent water/rock hexes; count distinct adjacent hexes, not multiple touching edges or an entire connected terrain area. These terrain requirements also apply when using a special enclosure. 5. Appeal and other ordinary effects resolve as each animal is played; after-finishing effects wait until the entire Animals action ends and the card moves.
answers.evidence: Animals action steps 1–5; cost reduced by 3 money per continent icon; special enclosure tokens; count distinct adjacent hexes; after-finishing effects wait.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II adds the option to play animals from the display within reputation range; pay an additional amount equal to the folder number. Hand and display animals can be mixed, and the display is not replenished until turn end. 2. At strength 5+, you may first gain one reputation at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies to animals played. 3. Animals II also permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: Side II: play ... from display within reputation range, paying ... folder number ... at strength 5 ... gain 1 reputation first ... may also play animals ... upgrade-required icon.

answers.answer: 1. Relocation is allowed only immediately when you build a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, once per new building; move all eligible corresponding animals that fit, choosing separately for each. 2. The new enclosure must satisfy each animal's terrain adjacency and have enough capacity. Mark each moved animal's indicated number of spaces with that many player tokens from your supply. 3. To free its old standard enclosure, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all that animal's requirements, including terrain. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied one meeting size; if none meets size, flip none. 4. Special-enclosure animals are relocated by adding tokens to the new enclosure; removing special-enclosure tokens is instead the release procedure.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals ... Only immediately ... all corresponding eligible animals that fit ... new special enclosure ... water/rock ... capacity ... flip smallest ... fallback ... add ... tokens.

answers.answer: 1. The four Association tasks are: reputation +2 (strength 2); partner zoo (strength 3); university (strength 4); conservation project work (strength 5). 2. Association I performs exactly one task; Association II performs one or more different tasks, with total task values no greater than action strength. 3. Each task needs an active worker. On a task where one of your workers is already present, place two workers instead; if three of yours are there, it cannot be repeated before the break. 4. Other players' workers on a task do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association action tasks strengths; side I exactly one; side II one or more different ... total value ... worker rules; other players' workers ... do not matter.

answers.answer: 1. Take a partner zoo or university from an available tile on the Association board and put it on the lowest empty corresponding space on your zoo map; take printed covered-space bonuses immediately. The zoo bonus also gives one continent icon and its animal-cost reduction; universities provide their printed reputation and research icons. 2. You cannot acquire a duplicate university; partner zoos must be from different continents, with a maximum of four, and the third/fourth require Association II. 3. A university is the only way to increase the hand limit, from three to five; the other university types leave it at three. At breaks, restock one of each partner-zoo continent and university kind except kinds already owned by every player, without adding duplicates.
answers.evidence: Gain partner zoo/university; lowest empty space; tile/reputation bonuses; cannot duplicate; max four and third/fourth require upgraded Association; hand limit 3 or 5; restock rules.

answers.answer: 1. Conservation project work (strength 5) can support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately; Association II can also play the new card from the display within reputation range for its folder-number additional cost. 2. Fulfill an uncovered condition/level with no player's token on it, then place one player token from the seven on the left edge of your map; each project can normally be supported by you only once. Each level holds only one token total across all players. 3. Take the token's activated map bonus immediately, before or after the project reward as you choose; recurring-marked bonuses repeat at every break. 4. A new card goes in the leftmost space above the board and shifts others right; if over the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project and return its tokens to owners' supplies, while their bonuses stay activated. Base projects below never move or replenish.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work ... support limits ... take 1 player token from left edge ... bonus immediately ... new card ... discard rightmost and return tokens to supply ... Base ... never move.

answers.answer: 1. No exact-size match is required: a release category 2− accepts printed standard requirement 1 or 2; category 3 accepts only 3; category 4+ accepts 4 or 5. The actual enclosure occupied or special-enclosure capacity does not set the category. 2. Lose only the animal's printed appeal before gaining conservation; discard the animal and lose its icons. Retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. 3. Playing a new Release into the Wild project gives one reputation; later support of a project already in play does not. 4. If the animal could use a special enclosure and its tokens can be removed, remove them; only otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none. Applies to flock animals too.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild projects ... 2− accepts size 1 or 2 ... lose only printed appeal ... playing a new ... grants 1 reputation ... remove tokens ... flip smallest ... fallback.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly one hand Sponsor whose level is no greater than action strength and whose conditions are met; alternatively advance Break by strength and take that much money. 2. Sponsors II may play one or more cards if strength +1 is at least their summed levels; X-tokens can raise strength. Cards may be from hand or an in-range display folder, paying its folder number; no refill until turn end. Meet conditions and resolve each card's instant effects before the next, except after-finishing effects. 3. If Sponsors II takes the break-track money option, it pays twice the money per strength. Thus, with one step remaining, the action still pays the full doubled amount even though movement stops at the track end.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I ... OR advance ... take that much money; Side II ... strength +1 ... hand or display ... pay folder ... after finishing ... break option ... money twice; full money even if token doesn't need all steps.

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit; clear Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock tiles; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Hand limit is normally three or five with the hand-limit university and is enforced at breaks. 3. Each kiosk pays one money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure and pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify, while empty special enclosures do. 4. If multiple players receive display cards during income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them) and refill the display after each player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure 1–6; kiosk income qualifying neighbors; display cards ... resolve clockwise ... refill after each such player's income.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation choose an Action-card upgrade or activate another worker; at 5 and 8 choose five money or a nearby Bonus tile; first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. If no one reaches 10, all discard one before scoring. 2. Game end is checked at the end of your own turn or during a break when your Appeal and Conservation counters occupy the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during someone else's turn waits until your turn end or a break unless another player triggers it first. 3. After an end triggered on a player's turn, every other player takes one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can add at most four conservation points. 5. VP equals your appeal minus the lowest appeal value in the scoring area of your Conservation counter; highest positive score wins. Ties go to the player with most supported projects, then tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Conservation track rewards; end of game check; appeal gained during another player's turn waits; final scoring cap; VP formula and tiebreak.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle nine Bonus tiles; put a random tile face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track (two beside 5 and two beside 8); do not use the two yellow spaces with icons and return the other five to the box. 2. The supplied quantity does not limit legal play: if a component runs out, use a suitable substitute, while explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability still apply.
answers.evidence: Setup: shuffle 9 ... four blank yellow spaces ... return remaining 5; Component supply: if a component runs out, use a suitable substitute.

answers.answer: 1. For advanced maps 1–8, either take two random maps and choose one, or lay out player count plus one advanced maps and choose in reverse turn order; return unselected maps. 2. Map A begins with an empty size-3 enclosure and a kiosk on its indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built and gets a kiosk tile reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A: Maps 1–8 ... take 2 random ... or lay out player count +1 ... Map A ... empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk.

answers.answer: 1. Put seven player tokens on the designated spaces at the left edge of the zoo map; these support conservation projects and each grants its bonus when taken. 2. Hire workers from the lowest supply space upward. 3. Some maps reward conservation points when you hire your last worker; Full-throated also takes the last-worker map reward if shown.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2; left edge holds the 7 player tokens ... Association worker supply: hire ... lowest ... certain zoo maps reward conservation ... last worker.

answers.answer: 1. Flip the chosen Action card from side I to side II in its current slot; it does not move. 2. Its improved action is usable from your next action. 3. It immediately counts as upgraded for conditions during the current action. 4. You cannot upgrade all five cards; there are four upgrades and one allows an alternative choice.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards: flip ... stays in its slot; improved action ... from your next action, while immediately counts as upgraded for conditions ... cannot upgrade all ...

answers.answer: 1. Cards I at strengths 1–5 draw/discard: 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1. Strengths above 5 use strength-5 column. 2. A required discard may be a newly drawn card or one already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw tables: Side I ... 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1; discard may be newly drawn or previously held.

answers.answer: 1. All seven animal categories count: bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. Bears and Petting Zoo animals count unless specifically excluded; bear may also have herbivore or predator category. Repeated category icons are not additional different categories for diversity.
answers.evidence: Animal categories (7) ... Bear and Petting Zoo animal ... included unless explicitly excluded; Species Diversity counts different animal categories.

answers.answer: 1. Association II may make exactly one donation per Association action, only if at least one Association task was performed that action; no worker is needed for the donation. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible and cover that donation space with a player token from your supply to gain one conservation. 3. Printed costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; setup-blocked spaces are skipped. Once all but the last are covered, each later donation costs 12 and places no additional token.
answers.evidence: Side II ... exactly 1 donation ... pay smallest amount still visible ... cover ... gain 1 conservation; printed ... 2,5,5,7,7,10,10, then repeatable 12 ...

answers.answer: 1. Zoo icons include only upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements. 2. Left-side card conditions and Conservation Project icons do not count; university reputation and hand-limit symbol are not zoo icons. 3. A card counts its own icon for its effects; double icons count twice and matching effects can trigger twice. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Shared principles: only upper-right card icons ... partner/university ... upper-left water/rock; conditions and project icons do not; cards count own icons; doubled icons count twice; card text takes priority.

answers.answer: 1. Count distinct water or rock hexes actually adjacent to the enclosure; multiple touching edges to the same hex count once. 2. A larger connected water/rock area counts only the hexes actually adjacent, not the whole connected region. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles are neither terrain spaces nor requirements.
answers.evidence: Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes ... touching one water hex ... one adjacency ... illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

answers.answer: 1. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants one reputation to the player who plays it; supporting an already-in-play Release project grants no such play bonus. 2. Breeding Program projects use the same condition for all three reward levels, so choose any available level that condition fulfills under the normal support rules.
answers.evidence: Release ... Bringing the project into play also grants 1 reputation; supporting it later does not. Breeding Program ... same requirement for all three reward spaces: choose any available one.

answers.answer: 1. In an effect written X:Y, X is the condition and Y the reward. 2. An unnumbered condition or one marked 'per' pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; when there are multiple thresholds, use the highest one met.
answers.evidence: For an effect written 'X : Y,' X ... condition ... Y ... reward; condition without number (or with per) ... once; numbered threshold ... highest one met.

answers.answer: 1. Connected means an uncovered space sharing an edge with a covered space. 2. Isolated means no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space has at least one of its six sides without a neighboring map hex. 4. 'Your zoo' includes your played cards, map and personal supply; 'any zoo' includes those things for all players.
answers.evidence: A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge ... isolated ... border ... 'Your zoo' ... 'any zoo' ...

answers.answer: 1. Place a unique building when playing its Sponsor, using its matching tile colored-face up; rotate freely but do not flip. 2. Follow ordinary placement rules and its water/rock adjacency requirement; it has no size-based construction payment. 3. It is not an enclosure, cannot house more animals, and is not water or rock terrain. 4. If it cannot legally be placed, the Sponsor card cannot be played.
answers.evidence: Unique buildings must be placed when playing their Sponsor: if placement is impossible, the card cannot be played. Use matching tile ... apply ordinary placement and terrain ... no size-based payment.

answers.answer: 1. Finish the Animals action, including moving its card to slot 1, before taking an animal's granted action. Use the named Action card normally and move it to slot 1 after executing it. 2. A named action such as Sponsors cannot be replaced by the X-token action; Determination grants any action and may choose the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Action / Determination: finish Animals, including moving its card ... Use its Action card normally ... named Action ... cannot be replaced ... Determination ... may choose X-token.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds the chosen project to hand; Dominance adds its named project from that deck. 2. Dominance does nothing if the named project is already in play. 3. Later play and immediately support the acquired card through Association above the board; it does not join the setup base-project row below it.
answers.evidence: Assertion / Dominance: search unused face-down base-project deck ... Dominance has no effect if ... already in play; later play ... placing it above the board.

answers.answer: 1. Resolve Boost and Clever after finishing Animals and moving that Action card. 2. Clever places the chosen card in slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. Boost places the named card in slot 1 or 5; moving it to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Boost / Clever: execute after finishing Animals and moving that card. Clever ... slot 1 ... Boost ... slot 1 or 5; moving to 5 shifts cards ... right left.

answers.answer: 1. Every affected zoo must have at least five appeal. Venom targets every other zoo with higher appeal than yours; Hypnosis and Pilfering target highest-appeal zoo(s), with ties chosen by the ability rules; Constriction targets other qualifying zoos ahead on appeal and/or conservation. 2. Eligibility is checked for the affected zoo; the animal's appeal can be awarded before or after its ability, so its new appeal normally need not count for selection. 3. The group may use the cards' solo replacement text for interactive abilities instead, without playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities. Eligibility ... at least 5 appeal ... playing animal's appeal may be awarded before or after ... multiplayer group ... alternative text marked for solo.

answers.answer: 1. Place Constriction tokens on highest slots: one token in slot 5 if target is ahead on one track, or two tokens in slots 4 and 5 if ahead on both. Never stack two on one card; duplicates return to supply. 2. Each token reduces affected action strength by two, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 3. Return used tokens after acting; unused tokens return at the break without effect.
answers.evidence: Constriction: ahead on one track ... one token (slot 5); ahead on both ... two (slots 4 and 5); never stack ... loses two strength ... each execution ... return ... break.

answers.answer: 1. At effective strength zero or below, you cannot use the regular action at that strength; use enough X-tokens to reach at least one, take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. The X-token alternative is unavailable if you already hold five X-tokens.
answers.evidence: At effective strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens ... use alternative X-token action, or leave the card until ... slot 3; Venom reference says X-token alternative ... fewer than five.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 lets you make up to two selections, deciding again after each whether to discard a display card and replenish it or discard a hand card then draw one deck card; you can change options between selections. 2. A display card discarded by Digging is replaced immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 ... choose up to twice ... decide again after each ... display card ... replaced immediately, shifting ...

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal avoids a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least its standard-enclosure size; that same host can support any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 2. A later non-flock herbivore cannot join the flock animal in that enclosure; without a qualifying host, house the flock animal normally. 3. On release, no proof of the flock animal's exact original accommodation is tracked; it still frees an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal: if another herbivore ... need not flip ... same ... any number ... Without ... normally; later non-flock ... cannot join ... exact historical residents are not tracked.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker, moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. Take any map reward for hiring the last worker if shown. 3. If all workers are already active, the ability has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated: activate lowest reserve worker ... Take a last-worker map reward if shown. If all workers are active ... no effect.

answers.answer: 1. Hunter reveals the specified number of deck cards and adds one revealed Animal card to hand, discarding the others. If none is an Animal, discard all revealed cards.
answers.evidence: Hunter X ... With no Animal among them, discard all.

answers.answer: 1. Choose among players tied for highest appeal; if the highest-appeal target is you, Hypnosis has no effect. The target must have at least five appeal. 2. Copy only their slot 1, 2 or 3 card and use its owner's upgraded/unupgraded side for the entire action; other upgrade conditions use your own cards. 3. Spend your own X-tokens, and move the borrowed card to slot 1 normally. 4. Venom and Constriction on the borrowed card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Hypnosis: choose ... among ties ... self ... no effect; copy only slot 1,2,3; targeted side ... own X-tokens ... move ... Venom/Constriction ... discarded ... Multiplier cannot be used.

answers.answer: 1. Put a gained Multiplier immediately on the named Action card; a bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any card. It permits executing the action twice in succession at the same base strength, moving the Action card only after both. 2. Each X-token boosts only one execution; after-finishing effects wait until both executions finish. 3. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the whole turn is finished, so it does not stop the second execution. 4. Used tokens return to supply; unused tokens are removed at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier: place ... immediately ... execute ... twice ... moving ... after both ... X-token boosts only one ... defer after-finishing ... break ... entire turn ... return used; unused ... next break.

answers.answer: 1. Two Multiplier tokens permit up to three executions, not four. 2. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens subject to the five-token cap, but you may not combine one X-token action with one regular action.
answers.evidence: Each additional Multiplier ... two tokens permit up to three actions, not four ... multiplied X-token alternative ... may take two ... may not mix.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking allows placing the Large Bird Aviary before Build II, but your zoo must not already have one and a legal site must exist. 2. Other placement restrictions remain, including Build II for upgrade-marked map spaces. 3. Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.
answers.evidence: Peacocking ... may place ... before upgrading Build ... no Aviary ... legal site ... restrictions ... Posturing ... normal placement ... one at a time.

answers.answer: 1. Petting Zoo animals give appeal successively: 3 for the first, 6 for the second and 9 for the third. 2. One Petting Zoo holds at most three such animals. 3. They count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Petting Zoo animal: your first grants 3 appeal, second 6, third 9 ... at most three ... count as small animals.

answers.answer: 1. Pilfering 1 targets the highest-appeal zoo; Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal zoo and the most-conservation zoo. 2. Choose among ties. The conservation leader must have at least one conservation point. 3. Self-targeting has no effect; if one zoo leads both tracks, it can be pilfered twice.
answers.evidence: Pilfering target reference; highest-appeal ... most-conservation separately ... conservation target ... at least 1 ... choose ties ... self ... same zoo ... twice.

answers.answer: 1. If the target can pay five money or has a hand card, they choose to give five money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. If they have no hand cards but can pay five, they give five money. If they have less than five money but a hand card, they give a card. If they have neither a card nor five money, they give all their current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X: target chooses ... five money or random hand-card draw ... no hand cards ... less than five ... neither ... all ... repeated ... sequentially.

answers.answer: 1. Pouch lets you tuck up to X hand cards under the animal for two appeal each; tucked cards have no remaining function. If that animal is released, discard its tucked cards too, retaining the appeal already gained. 2. Sunbathing sells up to X hand cards for four money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Pouch X ... tuck ... two appeal ... no remaining function ... if released, discard ... retain appeal; Sunbathing ... sold cards go to discard.

answers.answer: 1. An extra Final Scoring card from Resistance joins the cards available when you discard one at the first 10-conservation milestone. 2. At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card, each capped at four conservation points.
answers.evidence: Resistance: extra Final Scoring card drawn before 10-conservation milestone joins your choices when you discard one; at game end score every remaining ... each ... four-point cap.

answers.answer: 1. Scavenging shuffles the discard pile face down, draws randomly from it, makes the stated selection, then returns the discard pile face up. Scavenging 3 draws three random cards, keeps one and discards the other two.
answers.evidence: Scavenging: shuffle discard pile face down, draw randomly ... return ... face up; illustrated Scavenging 3 ... draws three ... keeps one.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; it does not allow a deck draw as an alternative. 2. Sponsor Magnet takes display Sponsors without a reputation-range restriction; if no Sponsor is present, it does nothing. 3. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping ... exactly one ... regardless of reputation; Sponsor Magnet ... need not be in reputation range; if no sponsor ... nothing; ordinary end-of-turn display refill.

answers.answer: 1. Venom tokens go on the affected player's lowest-slot cards, starting with slot 1 and at most one per card; duplicates return to supply. 2. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including when using the X-token alternative. 3. At turn end, pay two money only if you removed no Venom token this turn and at least one remains; if unable to pay, undo the turn and choose another action. 4. Unused Venom tokens are cleared at the next break without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom X: lowest slots ... one per card ... using ... removes ... Pay two money at turn end only if ...; cannot ... next break clears unused tokens.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian gives 2/5/10 money immediately for 1/2/3 universities. 2. Its recurring effect reduces conservation-project support task strength from 5 to 4. 3. Its final-scoring reward is one conservation for having three universities.
answers.evidence: 203 Veterinarian: I: 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities. R: ... strength 4 rather than 5. F: 1 conservation for three universities.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough counts projects previously supported by you, represented by tokens missing from the left edge of your map, and gives two appeal per such project when played. 2. It gives one conservation at each break.
answers.evidence: 206 Medical Breakthrough: I: 2 appeal per previously supported project (count tokens missing ...). B: 1 conservation.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research counts one conservation per pair of different continent/animal-category icons; research icons do not appear in this count. 2. For each conservation point you gain from it, every other player gets two money.
answers.evidence: 207 Basic Research: 1 conservation per two different continent/animal-category icons; each other player gets 2 money per conservation point you gain.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gives one appeal per research icon immediately. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Library owner gains two money. 3. Final reward: one conservation with five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: 208 Science Library: I ... appeal per research icon. R: whenever any player ... you, owner, gain 2 money. F ... five different animal categories.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives one appeal per Americas icon immediately. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk, subject to normal placement and spacing restrictions. 3. Its final condition is having at least five kiosks, for one conservation.
answers.evidence: 210 Expert on the Americas: I ... appeal per Americas icon. R ... free kiosk under normal placement and spacing rules. F ... five or more kiosks.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives one appeal per Australia icon immediately. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card under this Sponsor for two appeal; tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: 212 Expert on Australia: I ... appeal per Australia icon. R ... per Australia icon played ... tuck one hand card ... 2 appeal; tucked cards ... no further function.

answers.answer: 1. Each of Global Breeding Program and Breeding Program gets two supply tokens when played. 2. When supporting a base project below the Association board, return exactly one token to count as any one icon; never use both substitutes for one support. Base-origin cards played above the board do not qualify. 3. Final reward: one conservation with five or more project supports, counted by tokens missing from the left map edge.
answers.evidence: 215/218: put two supply tokens ... when supporting a base project below ... exactly one token as any one icon ... never both ... base-origin cards above do not qualify. F ... five or more project supports.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer allows each Build action to add one extra copy of a building built in that same action without extra strength. 2. Pay its normal money cost and obey placement rules; only one extra building is allowed even if several different buildings were built. Special enclosures still obey their one-per-type-per-zoo limit. 3. Final reward: five appeal for a fully covered map excluding water and rock.
answers.evidence: 217 Engineer: each Build action may add one extra copy ... without additional strength. Pay normal money ... only one extra ... special ... one-per-type. F: 5 appeal ...

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher immediately gives one appeal per water/rock icon. 2. It lets you cover water/rock spaces and ignore terrain requirements of animals and unique buildings; their printed terrain icons still count. 3. Covered terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist or Architectural Zoo; terrain need not be covered for a full map. 4. Final reward is two appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.
answers.evidence: 219 Diversity Researcher: I ... appeal per water/rock icon. You may cover ... ignore terrain requirements ... still count. Covered terrain stops counting ... F ... maximum three pairs.

answers.answer: 1. Each actual placement bonus on a border space triggers an additional choice of any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily on the border. 2. Multiple actual border bonuses can each trigger an extra choice, and the chosen bonuses may be the same or different; resolve in any order you choose. 3. Final condition: all building border spaces covered, excluding water and rock, for one conservation.
answers.evidence: 221 Archaeologist: Every actual placement bonus on a border space grants ... any uncovered ... Several ... same or different ... F ... all building border spaces ...

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording immediately gives one X-token. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives one additional conservation. 3. You may support the same release project repeatedly using different qualifying animals, but at most one token on that project per Association action. Each token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: 224 Migration Recording: I: 1 X-token. Each Release ... 1 additional conservation. May repeatedly support ... at most one token per project per Association action. Each token counts separately.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab immediately gives one X-token. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and identify the next qualifying player. 3. Final condition: all five continents, for one conservation.
answers.evidence: 225 Quarantine Lab: I: 1 X-token. Immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For latter two ... next qualifying player. F ... all five continents.

answers.answer: 1. Choose small or large permanently, mark that choice with a supply token, then reveal deck cards until finding an animal of that type; keep it and discard the others. 2. You cannot play animals of the opposite type. 3. Chosen small animals give two extra appeal; chosen large animals give four extra appeal. Size-3 animals remain legal but receive no bonus.
answers.evidence: 227 WAZA Special Assignment: choose small or large permanently ... reveal ... keep ... cannot play opposite ... chosen small ... 2 ... large 4 ... Size-3 ... legal but no bonus.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program immediately gives two money per small animal. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals qualifies for one extra small animal from hand, with normal costs/rules; mixing small and large animals prevents this. 3. Then add one small animal from the display to hand regardless of reputation; you may take it even if you declined the extra play.
answers.evidence: 228 ... 2 money per small animal. Animals action containing only small ... additional ... from hand ... add one ... display ... regardless ... may take ... even if declined.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives one appeal per water icon immediately. 2. Its recurring effect gives one money for each newly covered space adjacent to water, even if several spaces are part of one building; a space touching multiple water hexes still pays only once. 3. Final condition: all water hexes connected, meaning none isolated, for one conservation.
answers.evidence: 241 Hydrologist: I ... appeal per water icon. R ... each space newly covered ... one money ... each space ... only once. F ... all water hexes connected (none isolated).

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut is a unique building that must be placed when its Sponsor is played under ordinary placement rules. 2. Each bird icon played triggers drawing two deck cards, keeping one and discarding the other; the card's own icon counts if played as applicable.
answers.evidence: 249 Barred Owl Hut: Place the unique building. R: each bird icon played draws two deck cards; keep one, discard the other. Cards count own icons.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank is a unique building placed adjacent to water. 2. For each reptile icon played, its recurring effect lets you sell up to two hand cards for four money each; sold cards are discarded.
answers.evidence: 250 Sea Turtle Tank: Place adjacent to water. R: each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; discard sold cards.

answers.answer: 1. Each predator icon played triggers Hunter, with the number of cards revealed equal to your total predator icons. 2. A card with two predator icons triggers two sequential Hunters; count the new icons for the second Hunter as well.
answers.evidence: 252 Spotted Hyena Compound: each predator icon ... Hunter ... total predator icons. A double-predator card triggers two sequential Hunters, counting both new icons each time.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable enters with three supply tokens. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token to play a Sponsor from hand. 2. Pay money equal to that Sponsor's level and meet normal conditions. Its own herbivore icon can trigger this immediately when the Stable is played; there are three uses total.
answers.evidence: 253 Okapi Stable: place ... three supply tokens. Per herbivore icon ... spend one ... play a hand Sponsor for money equal to its level, observing ... own icon can trigger ... Three uses.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School gives one reputation and one conservation immediately. 2. Place its unique building so it covers at least two border spaces. 3. Take one in-range display card or draw one card from the deck; resolve its simultaneous benefits in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: 254 Zoo School: I: 1 reputation, 1 conservation, place ... covering at least two border spaces, take one in-range display card or draw one deck card. Resolve simultaneous ... chosen order.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance is placed on two border spaces and, unlike ordinary buildings, need not touch an existing building; other placement rules still apply. Later buildings may attach to it. 2. Its break income is two money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may be adjacent to a kiosk. 3. Final reward: five appeal with the map fully covered except water/rock.
answers.evidence: 257 Side Entrance: place on two border spaces ... need not touch ... later buildings may attach. B: 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; may stand beside kiosk. F ... 5 appeal ...

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals gives one appeal per connected uncovered building border space; water and rock are excluded. 2. At final scoring gain one conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces; evaluate each group separately and do not combine separate groups. 3. Upgrade-restricted spaces count even without Build II; water and rock spaces do not count.
answers.evidence: 260 Native Farm Animals: connected uncovered building border space (never water/rock); one conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces; groups separately; restricted spaces count ... exclude water/rock.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer immediately gives two money per different continent or animal-category icon; research icons do not count. 2. Each category or continent newly introduced to your zoo gives one appeal and two money. A double of the same newly introduced icon grants this novelty reward only once.
answers.evidence: 262 Explorer: I: 2 money per different continent/animal-category icon (research does not count). R ... newly introduced ... 1 appeal and 2 money; double ... only once.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program lets you place one size-5 standard enclosure free under normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, ignore one left-side condition, such as one required icon or the Animals upgrade; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute to ignore two conditions.
answers.evidence: 263 WAZA Large Animal Program: place size-5 ... free ... ignore one left-side condition ... Terrain ... cannot be ignored. Stacks with Research Institute ... two.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares your number of icons in each animal category with the player to your right and grants one conservation for each category where you have more. 2. If that player has none of a category, one of your icons suffices. 3. Maximum four conservation.
answers.evidence: Biodiverse Zoo (009): 1 conservation per animal category ... more icons than player to right ... if none ... one ... maximum 4.

answers.answer: 1. Observation Tower's bonus applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not to another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. Housing an animal in the qualifying standard enclosure gives the two appeal again even after an earlier animal was released. 4. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1 ... adjacent to tower hex itself ... special enclosures get no tower effect ... gives two appeal again after ... released. tower is not a building.

answers.answer: 1. Outdoor Areas qualifies a standard enclosure touching its own hex, not merely another water hex. 2. Such an enclosure counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; the bonus cannot be ignored on release or transfer. 3. It does not affect special enclosures, and the Outdoor Area is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2 ... touching Outdoor Area hex ... counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement ... cannot be ignored on release or transfer ... no effect on special ... not a building.

answers.answer: 1. A building on the space adjacent to Commercial Harbor activates it; the first building may begin beside the Harbor but need not. 2. Its discard ability can be used before, during or after your action, once per own turn, never during breaks or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4 ... building on its adjacent building space connects/activates ... first building may begin there but need not ... once per own turn ... not a building.

answers.answer: 1. Park Restaurant income is one money per adjacent covered hex, not per building; empty enclosures qualify, and each hex counts regardless of occupancy/type. 2. The Restaurant is not a building and does not count for kiosk income. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and follow other normal placement rules.
answers.evidence: Map 5 ... one money per adjacent covered hex, regardless ... Restaurant is not a building. special-enclosure placement bonus gives one ... free ... choose one, not both.

answers.answer: 1. Cover Hollywood Hills H spaces with buildings under ordinary placement rules. When an H is covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears; keep that Sponsor and discard the other revealed cards. 2. H is not a placement bonus, so it does not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three H spaces are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. Its bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner, and bonus buildings still need Build II for restricted spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8 ... cover H ... ordinary rules ... reveal ... H is not placement bonus ... after covering all three ... Sponsor level lower ... restrictions persist.

answers.answer: 1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its normal play conditions. 2. Play the card only from hand, even with Sponsors II; it cannot come from the display for this bonus. 3. The Sponsors Action card remains in its current slot and does not move.
answers.evidence: FAQ: bonus letting you pay money to play Sponsor costs ... requires usual conditions. Play it only from hand ... even if Sponsors upgraded. This ... leaves Sponsors Action card ... current slot.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; any gains beyond those track endpoints are lost.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Appeal cannot exceed 113, nor conservation 41; gains beyond those ends are lost.

answers.answer: 1. Venom affects every other zoo with higher appeal than yours; each affected zoo must have at least five appeal. 2. Hypnosis chooses a highest-appeal zoo with at least five appeal, choosing among ties; self-target has no effect, and it copies only slot 1, 2 or 3. 3. Pilfering 1 targets highest appeal; Pilfering 2 separately targets highest appeal and most conservation, with ties chosen, at least five appeal, and a conservation leader requiring at least one point; self-target has no effect. 4. Constriction affects every other zoo with at least five appeal that is ahead on appeal and/or conservation: one token if ahead on one, two if ahead on both.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference ... Venom ... Hypnosis ... Pilfering 1/2 ... Constriction ... threshold, slots and tokens.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal-card partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from the stated continent; a Sponsor-card partner-zoo condition permits any continent. 2. A red maximum-25-appeal condition permits play only while appeal is at most 25; the marker is only a reminder, not a general track cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least the printed reputation. 4. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one requirement from the card's left side, but not a terrain requirement.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Animal partner condition means continent; Sponsor permits any; max 25 appeal; minimum reputation; ignore-one-condition removes a left-edge requirement, not terrain.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 provides up to two selections. For each, choose either discard one display card and immediately replenish, or discard one hand card and draw one deck card; decide separately after each selection.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 ... choose up to twice between ... decide again after each ... display ... replaced immediately.

answers.answer: 1. After display cards are taken, slide cards from higher-numbered folders down while preserving their order. 2. Fill empty folders from the deck. The summary specifies that a Digging discard is replaced immediately by shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: After a turn ... move cards from higher-numbered folders down (keeping their order), then fill empty spaces; Digging ... shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures empty side up, showing the yellow border and size number. 2. Each placement-bonus space covered pays its bonus immediately, once; turning the enclosure occupied later does not pay those covered bonuses again.
answers.evidence: Place newly built standard enclosure empty side up ... each placement-bonus icon covered ... immediately once; ... does not award ... again.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches 10 conservation, each player chooses one Final Scoring card and discards it face down under the remaining pile.
answers.evidence: 10 conservation points: ... all players choose and discard one ... face down under the remaining pile.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; turns proceed clockwise, one player at a time. 2. Play has no formal rounds. 3. On a turn, take one regular action using one of five Action cards; additional effects or bonuses may grant further actions, which resolve according to their timing rules.
answers.evidence: Setup: randomly determine a start player; turn order clockwise. Turn Structure: no formal rounds ... on your turn ... one action using one of 5 Action cards.
